lawyer:
Md. Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate Instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellant
AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate instructed by Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent Nos.1-4
Not Represented ------ Respondent Nos. 5-21
parties:
Syed Shamsul Alam ------ Appellant
Vs.
Syed Hamidul Haque and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
The appellant as the pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.02 of 2002 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chittagong for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act-1950 in respect of the land transferred by the respondent Nos.5-10 in favour of respondent Nos.2-4 by a sale deed No.3326 registered on 17-10-2001 in the sub-registry office at Rangunia, Chittagong. 

 12. Mr. Md. Abdul Quayum, submitted that in this case, the trial Court upon consideration of the evidence on record reached to its decisions and allowed the pre-emption. He further submitted that the trial Court upon consideration of the materials on record found that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer tenant by inheritance in the case land and that there is homestead of them in the western 7 and 1/2 decimals of the case dag having 15 decimals. It was further held that the statement that the pre-emptor acted via media regarding the sale of the case land has not been proved. Moreover, the case was filed in time from knowledge of sale and there is no defect of parties. The fact that the pre-emptor by collecting loan and selling land filed this case has been admitted by the respondent preemptees which establish that the pre-emptor is in urgent need of the case land. The purchaser preemptees are strangers to the case land and on these findings, he allowed the pre-emption case. He further submitted that the Court of appeal found that the pre-emptor was offered to purchase the case land before the sale, but he did not purchase and, as such, he has waived his right of pre-emption and the pre-emption cannot be allowed. But this finding of the Court of appeal is not sustainable in law as the right of pre-emption accrues after the registration of the sale is complete. No action of the pre-emptor before the sale can bar him from the right of pre-emption. In this respect, he placed before us the case of Md. Dewan Ali vs Md. Jashimuddin reported in 13 MLR (AD) 198 = 60 DLR (AD) 73. But the High Court Division committed wrong in not considering this in its true perspective and discharging the Rule, which cannot be sustained in law. 

 14. Heard the learned advocates and perused the materials on record. It appears that originally the case holding belonged to Mir. Siddiq Ahmed and Syed Abdur Rahman and the heirs of Mir Siddiq Ahmed were the owners of eight annas of BS Dag No.12081 i.e 1/2 of 15 decimals and the remaining 1/2 belonged to heirs of Mr. Abdur Rahman. PW1 Syed Shamsul Alam, the pre-emptor in his evidence stated that the subsequent heirs of Mir Abdur Rahman exchanged western half ie 7.5 decimals of BS Dag No.12081 vide registered exchanged deed dated 7-1-1982 in favour of the preemptors side and the remaining 7 and 1/2 decimals of land of the eastern side is the case land. As such the pre-emptor are co-sharer in the case holding on the basis of inheritance and ewajnama. PW2 Haji Syed Hafijur Rahman in his evidence corroborated this by stating that the case land and the homestead of the pre-emptor are of same dag and the residence of the pre-emptor is at the west of the case land. The trial Court on consideration of this found that the pre- emptor is co-sharer of the case land of BS Dag No. 12081. On the other hand, the Court of appeal found that the preemptees are owners of the adjacent land of the case land in BS Dag No.12082. As such in this respect the claim of the pre-emptor stands. 

 16. Upon consideration of all the materials stated above we are of the view that whatever acts the pre-emptor has done, those were before the registration of the sale and that does not mean that he has waived his right of pre-empting the case land as right of pre-emption accrues on the date of registration of the sale deed and not before that the High Court Division committed error of law in dismissing the case of pre-emption and the prayer for pre-emption should be allowed resulting to the fact that this appeal should be allowed and the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4077 of 2004 should be set aside. Thus in the result, the Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No.02 of 2002 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Rangunia, Chittagong is allowed.
